To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

tolerance mechanisms in murine type 1 diabetes induced by anti-LFA-1/ICAM-1 mAb or anti-CD8 are not responsible for tolerance induction, indicating that there is an unknown mechanism responsible for the lack of capability of autoretactive T cells to destroy beta-cells in NOD mice.
the tolerance mechanism in murine autoimmune type I diabetes induced by anti-LFA-1 mAB and anti-CD-8 mAB are different.
tolerance mechanisms like deletion, anergy and Th2/Th1 cytokine shift were not responsible for the protection of autoimmune diabetes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the loss of autoreactive CD8 T cells and the induction of regulatory cytokines by anti-CD8 and anti-ICAM/LFA-1 treatment.
the development of a new therapeutic strategy for the treatment of human autoimmune diabetes.
the mechanisms of the tolerance induction by anti-ICM-1/LFA1 or anti-CD8 antibody treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tolerance induction in autoimmune disease is not a simple process and is not always achieved by the same mechanism, and that it is a complex process involving a variety of factors and mechanisms.
tolerance mechanisms induced by the short-term treatment with anti-ICAM/LFA-1 and anti-CD-8 mAbs during a critical period in NOD mice are not responsible for diabetes prevention.
a combination of several tolerance mechanisms may contribute to the protection from the onset of diabetes in NOD-ICAM-CD8-treated animals, but the exact mechanism remains to be elucidated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anti-CD8 antibody treatment induced a Th1/Th2/Th3 type of immune deviation and anti-ICAM/LFA-1 antibody treatment induced a type of Th1/Th3 deviation.
the tolerance mechanisms are not involved in this tolerance induction, and that the tolerance is mediated by the inhibition of the migration of autoreactive lymphocytes to pancreatic islet.

the loss of capability for autoreactive T cell infiltration and destruction of beta-cells is a consequence of the blockade of the T cell-endothelial interaction by antibodies against ICAM-LFA-1 or the blockade of T cell-CD8 interaction by anti-CD8 antibodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tolerance mechanism in the NOD mice treated with the anti-LFA-1/ICAM-1 or anti-CD8 is not clonal deletion, energy or regulatory T cells.
we have identified a new mechanism for the induction of tolerance, which is different from the previously known ones.
the mechanism of protection from autoimmune diabetes is different between the anti-ICAM/LFA-1 and the anti-CD8 treatment.
